C528/2178/2026
Dhirendra Kumar
--Applicant
 Versus
Mohd. Yameen
--Respondent
Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Vaibhav Singh Chauhan,
learned counsel for the applicants.
2. The present petition under Section
528 of the BNSS has been filed by the
applicant to set aside the impugned
summoning order dated 01.10.2018
passed by learned 2nd Addl. Civil Judge
(S.D.)/Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate,
District Haridwar and the entire
proceedings of Complaint Case No.12 of
2015 (New No.319 of 2023) under
Section 138 of the Negotiable
Instruments Act, 1881 pending in the
court of 1st Addl. Civil Judge
(S.D.)/Additional Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Haridwar.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant
would submit that, as per the complaint,
the applicant and co-accused Abrar
Alam entered into an agreement to sell a
piece of land and received consideration
from the complainant through cheque
and cash. Subsequently, upon

UKHC010178982026
2026:UHC:9245
discovering that the land was disputed,
the parties mutually agreed to cancel the
agreement, and the applicant allegedly
issued a cheque towards refund of the
amount received. The cheque was
dishonoured with the endorsement
"Exceeds Arrangement", and the
statutory demand notice was returned
unserved, whereupon the complainant
instituted proceedings under Section 138
of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
(hereinafter referred to as "the N.I. Act").
The learned Magistrate, vide order dated
01.10.2018, summoned the applicant
without proper appreciation of the
material on record.
4. Learned counsel would further
submit that the complainant had
disclosed that the applicant resided
outside the State of Uttarakhand.
Despite this, the learned Magistrate,
after accepting the complainant's
affidavit in lieu of his statement under
Section 200 Cr.P.C. and recording that
no further evidence under Section 202
Cr.P.C. was proposed, issued summons
without conducting the inquiry
contemplated under Section 202(1)
Cr.P.C. He would contend that the
impugned order is legally unsustainable
for non-compliance with the mandatory
statutory requirement of postponing the
issuance of process and conducting an
inquiry where the accused resides
beyond the Magistrate's territorial
jurisdiction. He would further submit

UKHC010178982026
2026:UHC:9245
that the applicant learnt of the
proceedings only in June 2026 and
thereafter took steps to seek bail.
5. Heard learned counsel for the
applicant and perused the material
available on record.
6. In In Re: Expeditious Trial of Cases
under Section 138 of the Negotiable
Instruments Act, 1881, Suo Motu Writ
Petition (Criminal) No. 2 of 2020, decided
on 16.04.2021, the Hon'ble Supreme
Court emphasised expeditious disposal
of complaints under the N.I. Act through
affidavits and documentary evidence,
subject to compliance with mandatory
procedural requirements. The principal
issue is whether the learned Magistrate
summoned the applicant, who allegedly
resides beyond the territorial jurisdiction
of the court, without complying with
Section 202(1) of the Cr.P.C.
7. Section 202(1) of the Cr.P.C.
mandates postponement of the issue of
process and an inquiry by the Magistrate
or investigation, as prescribed therein,
where the accused resides beyond the
Magistrate's territorial jurisdiction. In a
complaint under Section 138 of the N.I.
Act, affidavits and documentary evidence
may form part of such inquiry; however,
their mere consideration does not, by
itself, establish compliance. The record
must demonstrate the requisite inquiry
and application of judicial mind.
8. In the present case, the learned

UKHC010178982026
2026:UHC:9245
Magistrate considered the complainant's
affidavit and supporting documents
before issuing process. Whether this
satisfies Section 202 of the Cr.P.C.
depends upon the proceedings and
material on record. The objective of
expeditious disposal under the N.I. Act
cannot dispense with a mandatory
statutory requirement.
9. The other objections concerning the
statutory demand notice and the
underlying transaction involve matters to
be examined by the competent court in
accordance with law. No interference
under Section 528 of the B.N.S.S. is
warranted merely on the basis of
disputed factual issues requiring
appreciation of evidence.
10. Accordingly, the C-528 application
is dismissed. The applicant shall be at
liberty to raise all legally permissible
objections, including non-compliance
with Section 202 of the Cr.P.C., before
the learned Magistrate, who shall
consider the same in accordance with
law.
11. The observations made herein shall
not prejudice the merits of the case
before the trial court.
12. No order as to costs.
 (Alok Mahra, J.) 12.10.2026 Mamta
